messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@acme.com>, acme-procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-team: Fleet allocation matrix & deal prioritization (April 10)

Team — kicking off this week’s GPU fleet planning for committed/reserved deals and near-term expansion risk. Attached is the latest fleet_allocation_matrix_v2.xlsx (tabbed by week, pool, and deal priority). Key asks: 

1) Laura — can you confirm whether finance is comfortable moving D-4972 to Q3 billing cadence if we push reserved capacity to start in May? That shifts the revenue recognition and helps smoothing.

2) Karthik — we need an updated estimate for burst slots if ACME’s pilot moves from 2k to 8k concurrent tokens (scenario B in the sheet). Can you validate expected slot delta and whether existing pools can absorb short-term spikes?

3) Soojin — operational guardrails: what’s the minimum safety buffer we should hang on to for enterprise burst during lead-in weeks? Suggesting 10% but open to adjustments.

Marta/ACME — included you since we’ll likely need to move procurement timing depending on the slot sizing. If anything in the matrix looks off vs your forecast, flag it now.

Short meeting proposed Thursday 4/12 10:00 PT to lock the allocation decisions. If that time doesn’t work, tell me an alternative.

Attachments: fleet_allocation_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB); D-4972_MA-plan_v1.pdf (procurement summary, 85KB)

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — quick note from finance after glancing at the spreadsheet. Moving D-4972 to Q3 billing cadence is feasible, but we’ll need: 

- A signed MSA addendum by 5/1 to support the deferred start (procurement is on the thread).
- A revised invoice schedule attached to the HUB deal record (I can create once Ben confirms revised start week).

If we push recognition, cashflow models show a ~$420k shift from Q2 to Q3 (material but manageable). I’ll mark the deal as "billing change pending" in the forecast.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Ben/Laura — ran the scenario runs overnight. Notes: 

- Scenario A (2k tokens): current pools handle without any changes.
- Scenario B (8k tokens): we show +3 reserved slots needed for the ACME pool during peak weeks (weeks 19–24). That equates to ~3x our current burst window; we’d need short-term burst capacity or to shift other low-priority reserved pools.

Operational impact: burst credits will be consumed quickly; recommend the following mitigation steps:
- Promote deal D-4972 to priority level 2 (temporary) with a 6-week ramp to full reserved capacity.
- Pre-allocate 2 temporary burst nodes (estimated cost delta: $12k/week) while finance finalizes billing cadence.

I attached a quick export from the infra sim (excerpt included in the matrix tab). If ACME confirms the higher token profile today we’ll implement a temporary pool reassign on 4/15.

Karthik
Director, Fleet & Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

1) ACME confirms Scenario B (8k peak). Karthik to provision 2 temporary burst nodes starting 4/15; if we see sustained usage beyond week 24 we’ll convert to reserved slots.

2) Laura to mark D-4972 as "billing change pending" and prepare revised invoice schedule; procurement addendum target 4/28.
